scenes.narration: To isolate the term containing x, we subtract five from both sides. On the left, adding five and subtracting five cancel out, leaving just two x. On the right, thirteen minus five equals eight. This simplifies our equation to two x equals eight.

scenes.narration: Now, to completely isolate x, we divide both sides by two. On the left, two x divided by two leaves just x. On the right, eight divided by two gives four. So our final result is x equals four.

scenes.narration: So we arrive at our final result, x equals four. Notice that this is a pure number with no physical units attached, as we are simply solving an abstract algebraic equation. Whenever you solve for an unknown variable, always isolate it completely on the left-hand side. This clean final value tells us the exact number that satisfies our original equality.

Let's verify our solution by substituting x equals 4 back into the original equation. We write two times four plus five equals thirteen. When we compute the left side, two times four is eight, plus five gives thirteen. Since thirteen equals thirteen, our equality holds. Great work, the solution checks out!
